Proof

↗ lem:curve-shrinking-first-variation ↗ claim:curve-shrinking-curvature-inequality \sketch The first variation gives

\begin{equation} \frac{dL}{dt}=\int (-\Ric _g(S,S)-k^2)\, ds. \end{equation}

For $\Theta _\epsilon =\int h_\epsilon ds$, combine Claim 7 with the length-element variation. The $k^3$ term is canceled by $-h_\epsilon k^2$, and the integral of $h_\epsilon ''$ vanishes. Let $\epsilon \downarrow 0$.

□
